title: ProposalVerdictEnvelope
description: Output of the improve workflow's Verify phase: one verdict per ActionableProposal emitted by the reflector. The envelope shape is what the workflow gates on -- without a forced schema the verifier returned prose plus a fenced JSON block, the gate read `.proposals` off a string, and eight approved proposals were discarded as no_actionable_proposals.

verdicts.description: One entry per proposal handed to the verifier, in the order received. An empty array means nothing survived verification.

proposal_bead.description: Bead id the proposal is anchored to (echo the evidence_beads[0] value from the proposal).

verdict.description: approved = actionable and safe to stage; rejected = protected skill, insufficient evidence, non-applicable diff, or out of scope.

reason.description: Why this verdict. For a rejection, name the specific gate that failed.

target.description: Optional: file path the proposal edits, as verified to exist on disk.

category.description: Echo the proposal's category verbatim. The grader ranks on this and it is unverifiable when dropped.

mutation_type.description: Echo the proposal's mutation_type verbatim, so the category/mutation pairing stays checkable downstream.

priority.description: Echo the proposal's priority. Without it the Grade phase cannot produce the ranking it is asked for.

target_line_range.description: Line range this proposal edits, e.g. L20-L34. Required to approve two proposals that share one target file; absent, they are duplicates by rubric c4.

evidence_beads.description: Echo the proposal's evidence_beads so bead reality is checkable at grade time.

proposal.description: Echo the proposal text verbatim: the exact change to make. Rubric criterion 6 (actionable) is defined over this field and cannot be judged when it is dropped.

rationale.description: Echo the proposal's rationale. Criterion 5 allows a single-evidence-bead proposal ONLY when the rationale justifies it, so omitting this field silently fails otherwise-sound single-bead proposals.

notes.description: Optional cross-proposal observations that do not belong to a single verdict.
